# Open decisions from the 2026-09-15 session: all resolved by the operator

Resumed session, presented each open decision individually. Operator decisions below are
binding; where they differ from the prior session's recommendation that is noted. No
financial figures, per the local-only-report convention.

## 1. Wave 4 judging — HYBRID
Score Wave 4 against the existing reference set, then run a supplement panel over only the
Wave 4 findings not already in it. Preserves all 40 existing adjudications and closes the
sole-find blind spot, using the supplement mechanism already validated by the main-vs-
supplement precision convergence. Supersedes the prior session's "judge against the
existing reference set" recommendation, whose blind spot fell exactly on what Wave 4 exists
to measure: a finding Sonnet made that Opus missed has no reference entry and would have
scored as a false positive.

## 2. Sixth arm — gstack was ALREADY APPROVED; my framing was the error
I presented "evaluate gstack or stop at five arms" as an open question. It was not one.
ARMS_PROVENANCE.md records `garrytan/gstack` as "selected, feature fit pending" — an
approved arm awaiting skill selection, not a candidate awaiting approval. Corrected on
operator challenge.

## 3. Which gstack skill — plan-eng-review, after evaluating all four
gstack ships FOUR plan-review skills, not the two previously known. Evaluated against the
arm bar (reads a codebase / emits countable findings / can run unattended):

| skill | verdict | reason |
|---|---|---|
| plan-eng-review | FITS | 4-section review (Architecture / Code Quality / Tests / Performance), <=8 issues per section |
| plan-ceo-review | unsuitable | a scope EXPANDER: EXPANSION modes, "Persist CEO Plan", Accepted Scope / Deferred-to-TODOS |
| plan-devex-review | unsuitable | a 0-10 developer-experience RATING with persona interrogation and TTHW benchmarks; not a defect finder |
| plan-design-review | unsuitable | requires visual mockups and a design binary; corpus is backend/infra |

### Two recorded claims are WRONG and ARMS_PROVENANCE.md needs correcting

- "Fails on interactivity — AskUserQuestion is its control flow." All four skills carry an
  explicit `SESSION_KIND: spawned` rule: when spawned, do NOT call AskUserQuestion at all,
  auto-choose the recommended option, never BLOCKED. A sanctioned unattended path exists.
  It is gated on gstack's own `gstack-skill-start` preamble echoing that marker, so it
  requires INSTALLING gstack rather than vendoring one file — an integration task, not a
  blocker. The rejection was applied to the whole family on evidence from one member, and
  interactivity is gstack house style rather than a plan-ceo-review quirk.
- "Counts approvals rather than findings." True of plan-ceo-review. FALSE of
  plan-eng-review, whose emit format is
  `[P1] (confidence: 9/10) app/models/user.rb:42 — <one-line defect>`
  — severity, confidence, file:line anchor, description — plus a JSONL artifact written on
  every run even when zero findings. That is MORE machine-readable than any existing arm.
  It also ships a "pre-emit verification gate" aimed at killing a false-positive class,
  which makes it a substantive precision comparator rather than a makeweight.

### Note for harness integration
plan-eng-review WRITES its report into the plan file (the gate verifies the file ends with
`## GSTACK REVIEW REPORT`), so the arm must be given a disposable copy of each pinned plan.
SKILL.md alone is not the skill: it Reads `sections/review-sections.md` as its declared
source of truth.

## 4. gstack capability configuration — BOTH ON, run as shipped
plan-eng-review has two capabilities on by default that no other arm has: a web-search step
per architectural pattern (via `aside` or WebSearch), and an "Outside Voice" challenge that
shells out to an independent external model CLI. Both ship documented `unavailable`
fallbacks, so both COULD have been disabled without editing the skill.

Operator chose to run the tool AS SHIPPED, both enabled. Consequence to carry: gstack is
then the only arm with web access and a second-model opinion, so its recall and precision
figures require that caveat wherever they appear — the same discipline already applied to
mini's weaker model.

## 5. 36ab-b649-BLOCK corpus — RE-PIN AND RE-RUN
Operator chose to re-pin to the cleaned upstream ticket and re-run, against the prior
session's and this session's recommendation to freeze. Accepted consequences, stated once
and not relitigated: it invalidates the existing arms' runs and adjudications on that plan,
and gives up the only natural experiment in the corpus on how each arm handles a malformed
input. Practical note: this re-run can ride along with the gstack arm's pass over the
corpus rather than being a separate exercise.

## 6. Sonnet[1M] pinning failure — ACCEPT, AND VERIFY THE OPUS ARM'S CONTEXT TIER
Keep the plain-Sonnet runs. Evidence supporting acceptance: no Wave 4 run reports
compaction, context exhaustion or truncation. Per-run consumption of 265k-351k tokens is
cumulative across a multi-call agentic run, NOT peak context occupancy, so it is not
evidence of overflow.

The check that was NOT on the original decision list and is now required: confirm what
context window the Wave 1/3 Opus-5 superpowers arm actually had. If it was 1M while Wave 4
ran at 200k, Wave 4 varies model AND context budget, and the headline dispatch-compliance
result (7.5% vs 40%) weakens from "attributable to the model" to "attributable to the model
or its context budget" — a distinction that matters because compliance is about following
an instruction, which context size plausibly touches.

## 7. Wave 2 leftovers — RUN Q1 AND Q2, SHELVE Q3
Q1 (replicability) is load-bearing: the headline CE-vs-superpowers recall gap currently has
no known noise floor, so every comparison ships as a point estimate. Q1 produces that error
bar. Q2 (convergence) was never started and there is no `wave2/q2/` directory, but it reads
rebar's EXISTING sidecar history and needs no new reviews — shelving a nearly-free result
was the wrong trade, which is why this extends the prior session's Q1-only recommendation.
Q3 is shelved and written up as piloted-but-not-generalizable at n=1: one plan, with the
expensive arm already flat and non-converging at cycle 3.

## 8. Coverage panel scope — ALL 453 ISSUES
Not the four-arm 265. Two facts decided it. First, the engineering cost is identical either
way: the blocker is adapting `coverage_pack.py`, which reads `runs.json` and
`rebar_findings.json` covering 0 of 11 Wave 3 runs with null Wave 3 adjudication headers —
required for 265 as much as for 453, so only classifier passes scale. Second, the
homogeneity objection to pooling supplement-panel runs is undercut by this study's own
main-vs-supplement convergence, already cited as a consistency check. The panel's output is
a to-do list for rebar rather than a number in a comparison table, and for that purpose
coverage beats homogeneity.
